summary: @onereach/ts-memoize preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The npm preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime binary (pinned bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated script using a rotated string/constant array (WV8StW shift-rotator over n7gIxM) and hex-named identifiers. The package advertises itself as a TypeScript memoize decorator and declares main at./dist/cjs/index.cjs, but the published tarball contains no dist/ directory and would fail to resolve the advertised library entrypoint; only setup.mjs and math_init.js ship at the root, neither of which is in the declared files whitelist ("dist", "LICENSE"). Fetching a separate language runtime at install time solely to execute a package-local obfuscated payload under a non-Node interpreter — while the advertised library is absent — is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern and evades Node-oriented inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
